newsitem.title: USA: Japanese girl awaiting heart transplant dies.
newsitem.headline: Japanese girl awaiting heart transplant dies.

text.p: An 8-year-old Japanese girl awaiting a heart transplant at a Los Angeles hospital died early on Tuesday, a spokeswoman said.

Miyuki Monobe died of congenital heart disease at the University of California Los Angeles Medical Centre at 7:08 a.m. EDT (1108 GMT). "Everybody is very upset," hospital spokeswoman Ruthie Marek said.

The girl arrived at the hospital on March 29 hoping for a new heart, but she died before a suitable donor organ could be found, Marek said. She had been given "Status One" priority for the last 15 days on the United Network for Organ Sharing.
The girl suffered a heart attack on April 3 and Marek said at the time she was "very, very sick," in critical condition. She was placed on a heart-lung machine and remained on it until her death.

Monobe, who was born with a hole in her heart, came to the United States from her home in Shinagawa, Japan, looking for a new heart. Such transplants are very rare in Japan because of that country's organ donor laws.
Doctors at the hospital declared her a suitable transplant recipient but despite an exhaustive nationwide search a matching heart could not be found.
